title: Emergency Access identity: where users live, which IdPs, and how they sign in

prose.text: Emergency access users live in the identity provider, not in Private Access. {{users-not-stored}}

prose.label: Which IdP.
prose.text: {{idp-by-migration}} {{idp-arbitrary-domains}} Whether any other IdP type works is not documented {{gap:other-idps}}.
The settings these feed: [[zpa.emergency-access.configuration]]. What the page shows for each user: [[zpa.emergency-access.users]].

checks.do: Whether the tenant has migrated to Authentication Service, which decides the IdP, the prerequisites and which settings are hidden.
The IdP API token's scope, since users from any group it can manage appear and can be activated, deactivated or updated.
The email address for a plus sign, which can break a login hint.

users-not-stored.statement: Emergency access users are not stored in Private Access: the Emergency Access Users page lists users directly from Okta via the Okta API, or from Authentication Service when that is the IdP.

quotes: Users are not stored in Private Access. All users listed on the Emergency Access Users page come directly from Okta via the Okta API. If you are using Authentication Service, all users listed on the Emergency Access Users page come directly from Authentication Service.

idp-by-migration.statement: For end users who have not migrated to Authentication Service the IdP is an Okta IdP, and only Okta is supported; for end users who have migrated, Authentication Service is the IdP and only Authentication Service IdPs are supported.

quotes: you must create an Okta IdP in the Zscaler Admin Console, and you must create a group within Okta to designate the users for emergency access.
Only Okta IdPs are supported for emergency access.
If you are an end user that has migrated to Authentication Service, you must use Authentication Service as an IdP.
Only Authentication Service IdPs are supported for emergency access end users who have migrated to Authentication Service.

idp-arbitrary-domains.statement: The IdP shown on the Emergency Access page is the IdP that has Use with Arbitrary Domains enabled, and the field is read-only.

quotes: **IdP**: The IdP that has **Use with Arbitrary Domains** enabled. This is a read-only field.
evidence.after: For Private Access end users who have not migrated to Authentication Service

okta-prerequisites.statement: In Okta, the third-party user needs group administrator privileges, the email authenticator, and authentication policies.

quotes: The following must also be configured in Okta for the third-party user:
- Group administrators privileges. To learn more, refer to the Okta documentation.
- The email authenticator. To learn more, refer to the Okta documentation.

email-otp.statement: If the authentication policy uses Email One Time Pins, the invited user authenticates without a password by providing the OTP sent to the registered email address.

quotes: If the authentication policy utilizes Email One Time Pins (OTPs), then the invited user can authenticate in a manner that does not require a password by providing the OTP that was sent to the registered email address.

email-auth-required.statement: Email-based authentication is required for the user provisioned in Okta or Authentication Service, and the email that activates the account comes from the IdP or Authentication Service.

quotes: An email is sent from the IdP or Authentication Service to the user so that they can activate their account and authenticate. Email-based authentication is required for the user provisioned in Okta or Authentication Service.

branding-responsibility.statement: Customization, branding, emails and reply-to addresses are the organization's responsibility, and Zscaler handles only lifecycle management in the Admin Console.

quotes: It is the organization's responsibility to implement customization, branding, emails, and replies to email addresses. Zscaler only handles the lifecycle management in the Zscaler Admin Console.

auth-service-prerequisites.statement: For Authentication Service users, Arbitrary Guest Domains must be enabled, and the user must be in the Dynamic Group Guest Domains and Zscaler Emergency Access groups and assigned the Zscaler Private Access service entitlement.

quotes: Enable **Arbitrary Guest Domains**.
verify that the user is assigned to the **Dynamic Group Guest Domains** and the **Zscaler Emergency Access** groups in the drop-down menu.
Assign the user to the Zscaler Private Access service entitlement.

auth-service-hidden-fields.statement: With Authentication Service for users and User Single Sign-On enabled, the IdP API Token and Emergency Authentication Domains fields are hidden and the User Group Name field is disabled.

quotes: The **IdP API Token** field is hidden if you are subscribed to Authentication Service for users and User Single Sign-On (SSO) is enabled for your tenant.
The **User Group Name** field is disabled if you are subscribed to Authentication Service for users and User Single Sign-On (SSO) is enabled for your tenant.
the **Emergency Access Authentication Domains** field is hidden if you are subscribed to Authentication Service for users and User Single Sign-On (SSO) is enabled for your tenant.

token-permissive.statement: Private Access uses the Okta IdP API token to fetch the members of the designated group; a more permissive token shows additional users, and every user visible on the page can be activated, deactivated or updated even if outside the designated group.

quotes: If the specified IdP API Token is more permissive, additional users might be displayed on the Emergency Access Users page.
All of the users visible on the Emergency Access Users page can be activated, deactivated, or updated, even though they are not part of the user group designated for emergency access.

deleted-group.statement: If the designated group is deleted, users outside it are still shown while the settings stay configured, and if the credentials cover several groups, users of those groups continue to show.

quotes: If the user group designated for emergency access is deleted, users that are not part of the user group designated for emergency access are still shown on the Emergency Access Users page as long as the settings are configured.

plus-sign.statement: A plus sign in the email address appears as a blank space in the username field on the Okta login page when a login hint is used, and login may fail depending on Okta login rules.

quotes: Special characters such as plus symbols (+) appear as blank spaces within the username field on the Okta login page if you are using a login hint.
You might not be able to log in depending on your Okta login rules.

other-idps.title: Whether IdPs other than Okta and Authentication Service can be used
other-idps.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "Okta-only. No other IdP is supported ... No SAML IdP, no Entra ID, no generic OIDC provider." The help supports Okta, and Authentication Service for migrated tenants, and does not list unsupported IdP types. The legacy wording is corrected for Authentication Service.
